display.purpose: The login brand line. Appears exactly once in the product.

headline.purpose: The sheet name inside a title block.

title.purpose: A ruled section heading or chart header, always with its hairline rule.

body.purpose: Supporting prose and dialog descriptions. Rare.

label.purpose: Form labels, nav items, table cells.

annotation.purpose: The drafting annotation: every metric label, column head, and legend key. Tracked and uppercased under LTR only — Arabic takes neither.

figure.purpose: Every measured numeral. Tabular lining figures, direction:ltr with bidi isolation so a number reads correctly inside an Arabic sentence.

shadows.name: sheet-ambient
shadows.purpose: Available as --sheet-shadow for a surface that must read as lifted off the board. Used sparingly; sheets are flat at rest.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: A modal genuinely floats above the board.

shadows.name: tooltip
shadows.purpose: The chart's drawn tooltip, which tracks a cursor over content.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: The mobile rail over its ink scrim.

motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system; defined as --ease-draw on :root and used by every drawing step.

motion.name: draw-delay
motion.value: --draw-delay custom property; read as animation-delay by every drawing class
motion.purpose: The sequencing mechanism. Components compose the drafter's order by setting a start time; the stylesheet holds no hard-coded timeline.

motion.name: rule-in
motion.value: 340ms; transform scaleX(0) -> scaleX(1), transform-origin flips to right under RTL
motion.purpose: Step 1 and 3 of the inking sequence: a rule drawn along its length from the sheet's start edge. The section band's datum, the dimension cell's rule, the login panel's datum.

motion.name: strike-from-datum
motion.value: 560ms, default delay 140ms; clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0 0 0 0), mirrored keyframe under RTL
motion.purpose: Step 2: a quantity struck from the datum it was just ruled against. clip-path rather than scaleX so the 45 degree hatch keeps its angle.

motion.name: dimension-stagger
motion.value: --draw-delay: 340ms + i * 40ms, set per cell by DimensionGrid
motion.purpose: Step 3's capped stagger: dimension strings set out one after another across the sheet. Inherits from the cell wrapper to the rule inside it.

motion.name: plot-in
motion.value: 600ms, default delay 460ms; clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0 0 0 0), left-to-right in BOTH scripts
motion.purpose: Step 4: the plot traced last, as one drawing. Not direction-aware — the x-axis is time, so the drawing follows the data rather than the reading direction.

motion.name: ink-in
motion.purpose: The one non-drawn motion, for a surface arriving over the sheet rather than being drawn on it: the mobile drawer and the dialog overlay.

motion.name: pending-rule
motion.value: 1100ms cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) infinite; a 42%-wide 2px currentColor bar translateX(-100%) -> translateX(240%) along the control's bottom edge
motion.purpose: Work in progress drawn as a rule being ruled. Applied via [data-pending]::after, set by the Button's pending prop alongside aria-busy.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Every interactive state change, plus a 1px active press. Survives reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables .rule-in, .strike, .plot-in and .ink-in only; [data-pending]::after becomes a static 100%-wide bar at 0.45 opacity
motion.purpose: Targeted, not blanket. The sheet arrives complete while colour, state and focus feedback survive; the pending state stays visible and aria-busy still reports.

textures.name: hatch
textures.purpose: Open or unresolved region: remaining budget, empty states, skeletons.

textures.name: hatch-dense
textures.purpose: A solid consumed mass and an overrun. The cut through the material.

textures.name: hatch-value
textures.purpose: In dark the hatch and line work are drawn in amber — the blueprint reversal. The rail itself stays a filled amber field in both themes.

textures.name: board-grid

textures.purpose: The drafting board. Licensed only where the surface itself IS the board (a full-bleed empty half). Never wallpaper behind a floating panel.

narrative.overview:
The company mark is a building drawn in elevation — seven stepped storeys over a green ground-swoosh. This application is the rest of that sheet. Every screen behaves like a measured architectural drawing: quantities are drawn as mass, consumed quantity is a hatched cut through that mass, and zero is a green datum line that runs beneath every figure in the product. Numbers are not reported here, they are dimensioned — a label above, a measured extent with tick serifs, the figure beneath.

The system exists to refuse one specific thing: the SaaS card grid, where eight equal white boxes make eight unequal numbers look identical. Nothing in this world is a rounded card with a soft shadow. Surfaces are hairline rectangles — sheets — and each carries a title block naming what it is, over what extent, at what revision. Colour never scatters into accents: amber owns whole regions (the full-height navigation rail, the section band, the login's start half) and the green datum owns exactly one meaning. Density is high and deliberate; this is a back-office tool where a media buyer logs a period in under a minute and an admin reads a portfolio off one line.

Light is warm drafting paper; dark is blueprint ink. The two themes are not a tint of each other — in dark the amber stops being a wash and becomes the line work itself, the way a blueprint reverses its drawing. The rail stays a filled amber field in both, because identity does not toggle.
keyCharacteristics: Hairline rectangles, never rounded cards; the only radius in the system is 2px
Three line weights and never a fourth
45° hatch is the one texture, and it means "consumed" or "not yet drawn"
A 2px green datum that is zero, everywhere, on every surface that measures anything
Amber owns whole regions of the screen, never individual accents
Two typefaces: Alexandria for lettering, Archivo tabular for every figure
Motion is inking: line work draws itself in the order a drafter works, and text never moves
Arabic-first and direction-agnostic; every offset is logical

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: There are exactly three line values and never a fourth. `line` is the hairline that divides (rows, sheet edges, internal rules). `line-2` is the drawn edge that encloses (title blocks, fields, the section band's frame). `line-3` is the cut — full ink, reserved for the cut face in a section band, the heavy rule under a table header, and the doubled rule under a totals row. If a divider seems to want a new weight, it wants one of these three.

rules.name: The Datum Rule
rules.body: Green means zero and nothing else. It is never a success colour, never a brand accent, never a chart series chosen for variety. Every surface that measures a quantity draws the same 2px datum beneath it — the section band, the chart's reference line, the login's amber half, the empty state. A viewer who learns the datum on one screen has learned it on all of them.

rules.name: The Whole Region Rule
rules.body: Amber owns a region or it does not appear. Permitted regions: the navigation rail, the topbar below md, the primary button block, the drawn mass of a section band, the login's start half. Forbidden: a coloured left stripe on a card, a tinted icon, a coloured heading, a lone status dot. At md+ the rail carries the amber; below md the rail collapses into a drawer and the topbar itself becomes the amber band, so colour still owns a whole region at 390px.

rules.name: The Ink Set Rule
rules.body: Text on paper takes ink/ink-2/ink-3. Text on amber takes rail-ink/rail-ink-2 and dividers there take rail-line. The two sets never mix; the brand amber is a light colour and may not carry small paper-ink text.

rules.name: The Figure Face Rule
rules.body: Any numeral a user reads as a measurement is set in .figure — dimension cells, table numeric columns, chart axes and tooltips, date inputs, number inputs, revision stamps. A number that is part of a sentence is not a measurement and stays in the lettering face. Never mix the two faces inside one column.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Labels are annotations, not headings. Every metric label, column head, and legend entry is .annot. It carries the tracked uppercase treatment only under LTR, because Arabic has no case and rejects tracking — the class handles this; never hardcode uppercase or tracking-* on a label.

rules.name: The Logical Offset Rule
rules.body: Every offset is logical — start-*, end-*, ms-*, pe-*, inset-inline-*. No left/right in layout. The one exception, and it is load-bearing: CSS logical insets resolve against the element's own direction, and .figure sets direction: ltr. So a .figure element positioned with start-* lands on the wrong side of an RTL page. Two live bugs came from exactly this (a section band's percent reading, a date field's calendar button). When an element is direction-flipped, put the positioning on a plain wrapper, or use physical sides deliberately.

rules.name: The Visually-Hidden Pin Rule
rules.body: .sr-only is given inset-inline-start: 0; top: 0. Tailwind's own sr-only leaves the element at its static position, which inside an RTL flex row landed far outside the page box and stretched the document ~971px sideways, pushing the layout out of the visual viewport. Keep the override; not-sr-only still restores static position so the responsive sm:not-sr-only variants work.

rules.name: The Overflow Contract
rules.body: html carries overflow-x: clip and every content wrapper carries min-w-0. Wide content (schedules, charts) scrolls inside its own container with overscroll-x-contain; the page body never scrolls sideways.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Lit Rule
rules.body: Depth is a border and a tone step. Shadows exist only where an element is genuinely detached from the drawing surface — dialogs, drawers, cursor-tracking tooltips. A sheet, a title block, a dimension cell, a table, a form fieldset: all flat, all hairline.

rules.name: The Squared Rule
rules.body: Nothing is a pill and nothing is a circle. Buttons, tags, fields, tabs, avatars, and checkboxes are all 2px-cornered rectangles. A status is a squared tag with a hairline, never a coloured dot and never a rounded chip.

rules.name: The Board-Grid Rule
rules.body: .board-grid is licensed only where the surface it fills IS the drafting board — a full-bleed empty half of a screen. It is not wallpaper: never place it behind a floating panel or card, where it becomes decoration rather than material.

rules.name: The Hatch Rule
rules.body: Hatch means one of two things — quantity consumed, or region not yet drawn (empty states, skeletons). It never appears as ornament, and it never appears on a surface that is complete and full.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: A sheet's primary action lives in its title block, beside the sheet name. Not floating, not repeated at the foot, not duplicated in the rail.

rules.name: The Inking Rule
rules.body: The world's native motion is inking: a line appears along its own length, in the order a drafter works. The sequence is fixed and every surface uses the same one — the datum is ruled first (.rule-in, 340ms, so zero exists before any quantity), the mass is struck from it (.strike, 560ms, from 140ms), the dimension strings are set out with a capped stagger (--draw-delay: 340ms + i × 40ms), and the plot is traced last (.plot-in, 600ms, from 460ms). .ink-in (400ms, opacity plus a 4px rise) is the one non-drawn motion, reserved for a surface arriving over the sheet rather than being drawn on it: the mobile drawer and the dialog overlay. Every step reads its own start time from --draw-delay, so components compose the order and the stylesheet holds no hard-coded timeline. One curve throughout: --ease-draw (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)). State changes remain a 150ms transition on background, border, colour, and a 1px press.

rules.name: The Text-Never-Moves Rule
rules.body: Only line work is drawn. Every figure, label, and heading is legible at 0ms — no fade, no rise, no stagger on text. A dimension cell's rule inks in while its number is already readable beside it. If a new surface wants its content to animate, animate the rule under it, not the words.

rules.name: The Clip-Not-Scale Rule
rules.body: A struck mass is revealed with clip-path, never scaleX. Scaling shears the 45° hatch off its angle, and the hatch angle is the one texture in the system. Any future reveal over hatched material uses a clip.

rules.name: The Time-Order Rule
rules.body: rule-in and strike are direction-aware: they start from the sheet's start edge, so they mirror under RTL (transform-origin flips; strike swaps to a mirrored keyframe). plot-in deliberately does not — it sweeps left-to-right in both scripts, because the chart's x-axis is time and the drawing follows the data, not the reading direction. Direction-awareness is a property of the sheet, not of the plot.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: Reduced motion is targeted, not blanket. The four drawing animations (.rule-in, .strike, .plot-in, .ink-in) are disabled so the sheet simply arrives complete; colour, border, and focus feedback all survive, because a user who asks for less motion has not asked for less state. The pending mark stays visible as a static full-width ruled bar instead of a travelling one, and aria-busy still reports. Never restore the blanket * override that killed state feedback along with the drawing.

dos: Do build every screen from the six drawing primitives — Sheet, TitleBlock, DimensionCell, DimensionGrid, SectionBand, RuledHeading. A new surface should need no new container.
Do open every sheet with a title block naming it, its filter extent, and its revision.
Do draw the 2px green datum beneath anything that measures a quantity, and use green for nothing else.
Do set every measured numeral in .figure and every label in .annot.
Do keep to the three line weights: line divides, line-2 encloses, line-3 cuts.
Do let amber own a whole region — and below md, hand that region to the topbar when the rail collapses.
Do use logical offsets everywhere, and put positioning on a plain wrapper whenever the positioned element is direction-flipped (anything carrying .figure).
Do give an unresolved region a hatch and a dashed edge rather than a placeholder number.
Do keep the amber rail filled in dark mode; in dark, let amber carry the hatch and line work instead of the fills.
Do sequence a new surface's entrance with --draw-delay in the drafter's order — datum, mass, dimension strings, plot — and let every figure and label be legible at 0ms.
Do reveal anything hatched with clip-path, and keep plot-in sweeping left-to-right in both scripts because the axis is time.
donts: Don't ship a rounded card. 2px is the only radius; nothing is a pill or a circle.
Don't add a fourth line weight, a second texture, or a hatch angle other than 45°.
Don't scatter amber into accents — no coloured icons, coloured headings, coloured side stripes, or lone status dots.
Don't use green as a generic success or brand colour, or red for anything but a correction, overrun, or deletion.
Don't put amber (#e59731) behind small paper-ink text, or paper ink on an amber region — switch to the rail ink set.
Don't put a resting shadow on a sheet, title block, dimension cell, table, or fieldset.
Don't use .board-grid behind a floating panel; it is licensed only where the surface itself is the drafting board.
Don't use a native type="date" control — it prints the browser's locale segment order over an Arabic sheet.
Don't hardcode uppercase or tracking-* on a label; .annot applies them under LTR only, because Arabic takes neither.
Don't remove the .sr-only inset override, or overflow-x: clip on html — both hold the RTL layout inside the viewport.
Don't animate chart series individually; the plot is traced as one drawing, and Recharts' own series animation stays off.
Don't animate text — no fading, rising, or staggering figures, labels, or headings. Draw the rule, not the word.
Don't reveal a hatched mass with scaleX; it shears the 45° hatch off its angle. Use clip-path.
Don't hard-code a timeline in the stylesheet or invent a second easing curve; compose the order with --draw-delay and use --ease-draw.
Don't restore a blanket * reduced-motion override; disable the four drawing animations only, and keep colour, state, and focus feedback alive.
